children: WALL STREET INDEXES FINISH RED WITH RATES IN FOCUS

Wall Street's main indexes finished lower for the day and ended the week fairly close to where they started after Friday's jobs report blew past expectations, rekindling bets that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates this month.

Added to the strong jobs report was a threat from President Donald Trump to stop trade with some countries unless the Federal Reserve cuts rates. So it seems that the Fed may have to choose between either risking presidential ire if it raises rates in two weeks, or risking a hit to credibility, if it cuts or holds rates steady, after recent hawkish comments from Chair Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole.

On Friday, traders were pricing in a 58.4% probability for a rate cut in mid-September compared with 49.4% the day before, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. This marked a reversal of Thursday's move, when traders had cut their bets for a hike after Fed Governor Christopher Waller said that morning that he was inclined to be patient on rate policy while watching to see if price pressures ease.
Among the S&P 500 11 major industry sectors, only three gained on the day although the advances were small. Industrials
led the way with a 0.4% increase while technology
managed a 0.2% gain. In technology strength in the PHLX semiconductor index
countered a 2% drop in the S&P 500 software & services index (.SPLRCIS).
On the other side of the coin, consumer discretionary
was the biggest laggard, ending down 1.3%. That sector's biggest loser was Lululemon Athletica
, which tumbled 17.4% after touching an eight-year low. The sportswear maker's latest annual forecast cut prompted fears of a long-drawn-out overhaul under incoming CEO Heidi O'Neill.
Also in the consumer sector, Tesla
sank 5.9% after the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an investigation into whether the EV maker properly certified its autonomous Cybercab robotaxi.
For the week, the S&P 500
gained 0.09%, the Nasdaq Composite
rose 0.4%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average
fell 0.27%. The Russell 2000
small-cap index rose 0.11% for the week.
Here is your closing snapshot:
Wall Street indexes down, Dow leads losses with 0.9% drop
Cons disc down most among S&P 500 sectors; Industrials lead gainers
US dollar up ~0.2%; US crude settles up ~0.2%, gold falls ~1%, bitcoin off  >2%
US 10-year Treasury yields rise to ~4.78%
